```js
// A jigsaw: one image cut into nine, dragged back into place. Nothing moves
// on its own, so the only thing worth watching is somebody solving it.

let pieces = [];
let held = null;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(800, 600);
  noStroke();
  for (let i = 0; i < 9; i++) {
    pieces.push({
      x: 60 + (i % 3) * 230,
      y: 40 + floor(i / 3) * 180,
      w: 200,
      h: 150,
      hue: 20 + i * 24
    });
  }
  noLoop();
}

function draw() {
  background(12, 14, 20);
  for (const p of pieces) {
    fill(p.hue, 150, 90);
    rect(p.x, p.y, p.w, p.h, 6);
  }
}

function mousePressed() {
  for (let i = pieces.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    const p = pieces[i];
    if (mouseX > p.x && mouseX < p.x + p.w && mouseY > p.y && mouseY < p.y + p.h) {
      held = p;
      break;
    }
  }
  redraw();
}

function mouseDragged() {
  if (held) {
    held.x += movedX;
    held.y += movedY;
    redraw();
  }
}

function mouseReleased() {
  held = null;
  redraw();
}
```

```ghost
[
  {"t": 1200, "type": "move", "x": 0.2, "y": 0.25},
  {"t": 400, "type": "move", "x": 0.5, "y": 0.5},
  {"t": 1400, "type": "down", "x": 0.2, "y": 0.25},
  {"t": 1900, "type": "move", "x": 0.55, "y": 0.6},
  {"t": 2100, "type": "up", "x": 0.55, "y": 0.6},
  {"t": 2800, "type": "click", "x": 0.8, "y": 0.75}
]
```

## Statement

Nine rectangles that hold still until a hand arrives, then go wherever it puts
them. I wrote the pointer script from the two gestures I actually tested: pick
up the top-left piece, carry it to the middle, let go, and tap the one in the
corner to show that a click alone does nothing but choose.
